pull.title: fix(reasoning): a toggle-only model on an effort-only host sends the user's rung, and the richer stated record wins across catalogue rungs
pull.body:
## A toggle-only model on an effort-only host sends the level you asked for again

Since 6.3.0, a model whose only reasoning knob is an on/off switch, sitting behind a gateway whose only way of saying "reason" is one of its own effort words, has been sent **nothing at all**. This restores the instruction — as the level *you* asked for, clamped to that host's own scale — and stops the dashboard badging the correct "nothing was sent" case as a defect.

## What was wrong

**1. One host, two answers.** `_channels` narrows the toggle channel when a host's "on" value is written into its own effort field. That narrowing is right: `NamedEffortReasoning(enabled_value="max")` is a default rung, not a switch, and answering a request for `low` with the host's `max` was a real regression. But only one of the three consumers was taught what to do next. `_drop_controls` read the *unnarrowed* `dialect.toggle` and still emitted the on-value; `_adapt_budget` read `default_rung` and still emitted it; `_adapt_effort` read the narrowed `channels.toggle`, fell through, and returned "send nothing".

Measured on the running install since 6.4.0, route `commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free`:

```
38 requests, every one:  requested control=on, effort=max
                         reasoning_adaptation_kind = 'dropped'
                         reasoning_emitted        = 0
captured wire keys:      [max_tokens, messages, model, stream, stream_options, tools]
```

No reasoning key of any kind, where 5.73.0 sent `reasoning_effort: max`.

**2. One adaptation kind meant two incompatible things.** `DROPPED` was returned both where a reasoning key *is* sent (the level was discarded, thinking switched on through another field) and where nothing at all leaves. The dashboard's `wireContradicts` badges a row **"gating asked for reasoning; nothing was sent"** when `reasoning_emitted === 0` and the kind is `substituted|clamped|dropped` — so all 38 rows above, the correct and intended outcome, wore that badge falsely.

**3. The catalogue produced a record it forbids elsewhere.** `_cross_provider_capability` reconciles "this model has no effort knob" against a stated list of effort words, because the two are one statement. `_reference_then_vote_capability` merges the reference row and the vote *after* that reconciliation and never re-runs it, so `commandcode/openai/o3` resolved:

```
supports_effort_control = False                 (OpenRouter catalogue, tier 5)
supported_efforts       = {low, medium, high}   (cross-provider, tier 7)
```

`anthropic/claude-opus-4.5` was identical. Gating then read "no effort control" beside a vocabulary nothing would ever consult.

**4. A stated OpenRouter `False` beat a three-plus-row cross-provider `True`, always** — `merge_reasoning_capabilities` treats the primary's `False` as a real answer, which is correct for that function and wrong as the entire tie-break.

## What to expect now

| host class | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| on-signal **is** the effort field (`commandcode`, `groq`, `cerebras`, `sambanova`, `nararoute`, `cohere`, `wafer`, `fireworks`, `ollama`, `ollama_cloud`) — toggle-only model at `max` | *(no reasoning key)* | `{"reasoning_effort": "max"}` where the host's enum has `max`; `{"reasoning_effort": "high"}` where it stops at `high` (kind `clamped`) |
| the same, at `low` | *(no reasoning key)* | `{"reasoning_effort": "low"}` — the host's own `max` is still **never** substituted for a level you named |
| host with a real on/off field (`open_router`, `nous_portal`, `kilo`, `zai`, `cloudflare`, NIM) | `{"reasoning": {"enabled": true}}` etc. | **unchanged** — the honest toggle path is better than a rung and keeps priority |
| host with no reasoning field at all, and every default-dialect host (`toggle=False`) | *(nothing)*, kind `dropped` | *(nothing)*, kind **`nothing_sent`** — same wire, honest label, no false badge |
| effort-capable model anywhere | clamp to the shared vocabulary | **unchanged** |
| any numeric limit | tightest rung | **unchanged, and now guarded by a test** |

**Resolution.** For a provider models.dev has no section of its own for, the three reasoning-*control* fields now resolve to the more capable of the two stated records, and the Models page reports the rung that actually won each field — so one model can honestly read "cross-provider, exact id" on one field beside "OpenRouter catalogue, exact id" on another. `can_reason`, `mandatory` and `default_enabled` stay reference-first. The quorum is unchanged (`MIN_APPROXIMATE_BOOLEAN_REPORTERS` / `..._VOCABULARY_REPORTERS` are still 3): this chooses between two records that have each already cleared their own bar, and a single stray row still cannot win anything.

**56 routes** change their resolved reasoning capability on the current 4.8 MB cache (the count moves as the cache refreshes). Compactly, the affected names:

```
amazon/nova-2-lite-v1, anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5, anthropic/claude-opus-4.5,
anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5, claude-haiku-4.5, claude-opus-4.5, claude-sonnet-4.5,
deepseek-chat-v3.1, deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1,
deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06,
gemini-3-pro-image, google/gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06, google/gemini-3-pro-image,
grok-4.20, ling-3.0-flash, nemotron-3.5-lightning, nemotron-3.5-lightning:free,
nex-agi/nex-n2-mini, nex-agi/nex-n2-pro, nex-n2-mini, nex-n2-pro, nova-2-lite-v1,
nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning, nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free, o1, o1-pro, o3,
o3-mini, o3-pro, o4-mini, openai/o1, openai/o1-pro, openai/o3, openai/o3-mini,
openai/o3-pro, openai/o4-mini, perplexity/sonar-reasoning-pro, qwen/qwen3-14b,
qwen/qwen3.8-flash, qwen/qwen3.8-max, qwen3-14b, qwen3-8b, qwen3.8-flash,
qwen3.8-max, solar-pro4, sonar-deep-research, sonar-reasoning-pro, step-3.5-flash,
stepfun/step-3.5-flash, upstage/solar-pro4, x-ai/grok-4.20, x-ai/grok-build-0.1,
xiaomi/mimo-v2.5-pro
```

Typical shape: `eff=False` (tier 5) → `eff=True` (tier 7), which also removes the self-contradiction in #3. **The four routes the investigation named are all unchanged** — `commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free`, `commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free`, `nvidia_nim/moonshotai/kimi-k3` — and the live defect is fixed entirely by the gating half. The two `opencode`/`nvidia_nim` routes have their own models.dev bucket, so the tie-break cannot reach them by construction; that is asserted, not merely observed.

## Live evidence

Through the real gating and the real provider encoders, keys read from `~/.fcc/.env` and never printed:

```
commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free @ max
  resolved: can=True eff=False tog=True bud=False vocab=None  (tiers: all 6)
  adaptation: unchanged
  wire: {"reasoning_effort": "max"}   status=200  reasoning_tokens=0

commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free @ low          <- the regression guard, live
  wire: {"reasoning_effort": "low"}   status=200  reasoning_tokens=0

commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash @ max               <- unchanged control
  wire: {"reasoning_effort": "max"}   status=200  reasoning_tokens=137

opencode/mimo-v2.5-free @ high
  resolved: no control at all -> _drop_controls -> {} , kind nothing_sent
  status=429 FreeUsageLimitError (free tier), so the 400 path was not exercised live
```

## Dashboard, verified in a real browser

A harness on `:8099` served this branch's `admin_static` against the running 6.4.0 install's data (GETs only; writes stubbed, never forwarded). On a real stored row — `commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free`, `reasoning_adaptation_kind = "dropped"`, `reasoning_emitted = false`:

- the **"gating asked for reasoning; nothing was sent" badge is gone**;
- the wire line reads `no reasoning instruction sent (model default applies)`;
- the adaptation row still names the rung, verbatim: `REASONING LEVEL DROPPED: 'commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free' has an on/off switch only and this host has no on/off field; sending no reasoning instruction -- the model's own default applies -- instead of effort 'max'`.

A real `substituted` row with an empty wire **still shows the badge**, so the true positive survives. In-page, `wireContradicts` at `reasoning_emitted: 0` returns `false` for `nothing_sent` and `dropped`, `true` for `clamped` and `substituted`. No console errors on either page.

The Models page renders `commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free` cleanly: `can reason yes` / `effort no` / `toggle yes` / `budget no`, all at "tier 6 of 11 — OpenRouter catalogue, tag stripped", beside the host dialect `effort via reasoning_effort: high, low, max, medium, xhigh · on/off via reasoning_effort · no thinking-budget field · cannot be switched off`. Its 7-day chip reads `reasoning requested 20/6808, returned 0/6808` — the measurement that will show whether this gateway ever starts forwarding it.

## Action required

**None.** No new setting, no renamed environment variable, no migration.

## Known and deliberate

- **Command Code still returns `reasoning_tokens=0` for `minimax/minimax-m3-free`.** It did so under every body shape probed before this change, including `reasoning:{enabled:true}` and `chat_template_kwargs`. This PR restores a correct *request*; whether that gateway forwards it to a model that acts on it is the gateway's business. The requested-vs-returned column added in 6.4.0 is what will say so. **Do not read this as a thinking improvement — it was not measured as one.**
- **Historic rows are not migrated.** A row written before this version means what it meant when it was written, so the dashboard will show both `dropped` and `nothing_sent` for the same pre-6.6.0 situation. That is intended, not a bug.
- **`"dropped"` was removed from the badge list rather than `"nothing_sent"` being added to it.** Because stored rows are not migrated, a stored `dropped` is ambiguous between the two senses, and on the live install the correct sense was the overwhelming majority. The cost is that a post-6.6.0 genuine `dropped` contradiction is no longer badged; a false alarm on working behaviour is worse than a missed one on a case the adaptation message already spells out. `substituted` and `clamped` are unambiguous in both versions and still badge.
- **`_drop_controls` deliberately keeps the host's on-value.** A toggle-only model asking for `low` now gets `low`; a model that publishes *no* control still gets the host's on-signal. The first told us it has a switch, so a rung is the nearest legal thing to the ask; the second told us it has neither a switch nor a scale. The asymmetry is intentional and has a test that says so.
- **The `_channels` narrowing is not reverted.** "Revert the narrowing" is the obvious wrong fix; this PR fixes its consequence.
- The tie-break is **not** extended to `can_reason` (inverting a curated "does not reason" would send reasoning to a model that has none) or to the provider-payload rungs 1-2 (a provider's own `/models` is a statement about *this deployment*, not about the model).

## Residual risks

1. **A host that forwards the rung to a model that rejects it pays one 400 per model, per provider generation.** The reject-and-remember net added in 6.5.0 is the backstop: it strips the field the host's own 400 names, retries once, and never sends it for that model again. Because the table is instance-scoped (exactly like the learned output cap), a config reload re-pays it once. Deliberate.
2. **The catalogue's "richer" record can overstate a deployment.** A model that genuinely has no effort control on *this* host, described by three other hosts that do, will now be sent the field. Three backstops: the reject-and-remember net; the requested-vs-returned column, where an operator can see the field went out and nothing came back; and the per-model parameter override, applied after every postprocessor, which can pin or null `reasoning_effort`.
3. **Fixing the wire is not the same as making a model think.** See "Known and deliberate".
4. **The new kind is a UI-visible enum change.** Any consumer keying on `dropped` that the grep did not find will silently stop matching the rows that became `nothing_sent`. The grep found exactly one — the badge list; the kind has no label map and is never rendered as a pill, only the adaptation *message* is shown.
5. **Tier reporting on the Models page moves for the affected routes.** A field that said "OpenRouter catalogue, exact id" may now say "cross-provider, exact id". That is more honest and less reassuring, and an operator who has learned to trust the tier-5 label will read it as a downgrade when the answer itself did not get worse.
6. **`_Channels` gains a third overlapping boolean.** `toggle`, `default_rung` and `on_signal_is_the_effort_field` now describe one host's on-signal, and reading the wrong one is precisely what shipped the defect this PR fixes. The docstring is the mitigation and was written with that in mind.
7. **`UNCHANGED` with no message hides a real pass-through from the request log.** A toggle-only model whose rung passes through unclamped produces no adaptation row; the operator learns what happened from the recorded wire value. Relaxing `ReasoningAdaptation`'s "`message is None` iff `UNCHANGED`" invariant to fix that would break every consumer's "a message means something changed" assumption, so it was not done.

## Baseline note

The local suite has **15** pre-existing failures that also fail on unmodified `main`: 8 websearch / `test_web_server_tools` tests that read the real `~/.fcc/.env`, 6 PowerShell installer tests, and `tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`. GitHub runners have no `~/.fcc`, so they pass there. Nothing to chase.

commit.message:
fix(reasoning): a toggle-only model on an effort-only host sends the user's rung, and the richer stated record wins across catalogue rungs (#G)

Four defects, one shipped wire and one shipped dashboard badge.

**A host's on-signal was disqualified for one caller and not the others.**
`_channels` correctly narrows the toggle channel when a host's "on" value is
written into its own effort field -- `NamedEffortReasoning(enabled_value="max")`
is a default rung, not a switch, and answering a request for `low` with the
host's `max` is the regression that narrowing removed. But only one of the
three consumers was given a next step. `_drop_controls` read the unnarrowed
`dialect.toggle` and still emitted the on-value; `_adapt_budget` read
`default_rung` and still emitted it; `_adapt_effort` read the narrowed
`channels.toggle`, fell through, and returned `provider_default()` -- nothing at
all. Three paths meaning "the level cannot be honoured, keep thinking on"
resolved one host two different ways. Measured on the live install since 6.4.0:
`commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free`, 38 requests, every one
`requested control=on effort=max`, every one `reasoning_adaptation_kind=dropped`
and `reasoning_emitted=0`, captured wire keys
`[max_tokens, messages, model, stream, stream_options, tools]` -- no reasoning
key of any kind, where 5.73.0 sent `reasoning_effort: max`.

**One adaptation kind meant two incompatible things, and the badge read it.**
`DROPPED` was returned both where a reasoning key IS sent (the level was
discarded, thinking switched on through another field) and where nothing at all
is sent. `admin.js`'s `wireContradicts` badges a row as a wire contradiction
when `reasoning_emitted === 0` and the kind is `substituted|clamped|dropped`, so
all 38 rows above -- the correct, intended outcome -- were badged as a defect.

**The catalogue produced a record it forbids elsewhere.**
`_cross_provider_capability` explicitly reconciles "no effort knob" against a
stated effort vocabulary, because the pair is one statement. But
`_reference_then_vote_capability` merges the reference row and the vote *after*
that reconciliation and never re-runs it, so `commandcode/openai/o3` resolved
`supports_effort_control=False` at tier 5 beside `supported_efforts={low,medium,high}`
at tier 7. Gating then read `channels.effort=False` while `effort_values` held a
vocabulary nothing would ever consult. `anthropic/claude-opus-4.5` was identical.

**And a stated OpenRouter `False` beat a three-plus-row cross-provider `True`,
always,** because `merge_reasoning_capabilities` treats `primary`'s `False` as a
real answer -- correct for that function, wrong as the whole tie-break.

The rule now:

- A model that publishes only an on/off switch, on a host whose only way of
  saying "reason" is one of its own effort rungs, is sent **the caller's own
  rung**, clamped to the host's enum: `max` stays `max` on Command Code, folds
  to `high` on a low/medium/high host. The host's `enabled_value` is still never
  substituted for a level the caller named -- `low` leaves as `low`.
- A host with no reasoning field at all still sends nothing, now reported as the
  new `NOTHING_SENT` kind. The honest toggle paths (the OpenRouter
  `reasoning.enabled` object, `thinking`, `chat_template_kwargs`) are unchanged
  and still take priority wherever the host has one.
- `_drop_controls` and `_adapt_budget` report `DROPPED` where thinking was
  enabled through a field the host has, `NOTHING_SENT` where nothing left.
- For a provider models.dev has no bucket for, the three reasoning-*control*
  fields resolve to the more capable stated record and the reported rung follows
  the winner. `can_reason`, `mandatory` and `default_enabled` stay
  reference-first, and numeric limits are a different function and are untouched.

Non-obvious choices, each of which a reviewer will ask about:

- **The caller's rung, not the host's default rung.** It is more thinking than
  nothing and it invents no rung: the number that leaves is the number that was
  asked for, moved only as far as the host's own enum forces. The narrowing in
  `_channels` is right and is not reverted -- this fixes its consequence.
- **`_drop_controls` is deliberately NOT given the same treatment.** A
  toggle-only model asking for `low` now gets `low`; a model that publishes no
  control at all still gets the host's on-value. The first told us it has a
  switch, so a rung is the nearest legal thing to the ask; the second told us it
  has neither a switch nor a scale, so the level was genuinely un-honourable.
  The asymmetry is intentional and is pinned by a test that says so.
- **The pass-through case logs at INFO and reports `UNCHANGED` with no message.**
  `ReasoningAdaptation` documents `message is None` exactly when the kind is
  `UNCHANGED`; prose on an `UNCHANGED` would break every consumer's "a message
  means something changed" assumption. The operator still sees the value,
  because the wire capture records it.
- **`"dropped"` is removed from the badge list rather than `"nothing_sent"`
  being added to it.** Stored rows are deliberately not migrated -- a row means
  what it meant when it was written -- so every pre-6.6.0 `dropped` row is
  ambiguous between the two senses, and on the live install the correct sense
  was the overwhelming majority. A false alarm on working behaviour is worse
  than a missed one on a case the adaptation message already describes in full.
  `substituted` and `clamped` are unambiguous in both versions and still badge.
- **Prefer-richer is scoped to the four reasoning-control fields, never to a
  numeric limit, and the quorum is unchanged** (`MIN_APPROXIMATE_*_REPORTERS`
  stays 3). It chooses between two records that have each already cleared their
  own bar; a single stray row still cannot win anything.

Verification, all run:

- `uv run ruff format`, `uv run ruff check --fix`, repo-wide `uv run ty check`
  (all pass), the suppression grep-ban (clean).
- Resolution survey against the real 4.8 MB models.dev cache: 56 bucket-less
  routes change their resolved reasoning capability, 0 records are left claiming
  no effort control beside a stated vocabulary (previously the `openai/o3` shape
  above), and `model_output_limit_tiered` returns the same number at the same
  tier 5 for every route whose reasoning fields moved.
- The four routes the investigation named are all unchanged, as predicted:
  `commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free`, `commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`,
  `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` and `nvidia_nim/moonshotai/kimi-k3`. The live defect
  is fixed entirely by the gating half.
- **Live, through the real gating and the real provider encoders** (keys read
  from `~/.fcc/.env`, never printed):
  `commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free` at `max` now puts
  `{"reasoning_effort": "max"}` on the wire, HTTP 200 -- and at `low` puts
  `{"reasoning_effort": "low"}`, HTTP 200, which is the regression guard live.
  **`reasoning_tokens` is still 0 on that route**, as it was under every body
  shape probed before this change: this gateway does not forward reasoning for
  that model, and fixing the request is not a claim that the model will think.
  `commandcode/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` at `max` is unchanged and returned 200 with
  `reasoning_tokens=137`. `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` resolves to no-control (not
  toggle-only), so it takes `_drop_controls`, sends `{}` and now reports
  `NOTHING_SENT`; its free tier answered 429 `FreeUsageLimitError`, so the
  400-strip-retry-learn sequence could not be exercised live and is covered by
  tests instead.
- The dashboard was driven in a real browser (a harness on :8099 serving this
  branch's admin_static against the running 6.4.0 install's data, GETs only).
  A real minimax row stored as `dropped` with `reasoning_emitted=0` now shows
  NO contradiction badge, and its wire line reads "no reasoning instruction
  sent (model default applies)". A real `substituted` row with an empty wire
  still DOES show the badge, so the true positive survives. In-page:
  `wireContradicts` at `reasoning_emitted: 0` is false for `nothing_sent` and
  `dropped`, true for `clamped` and `substituted`. No console errors.

Deliberately not done: historic rows are not migrated, so the dashboard shows
both `dropped` and `nothing_sent` for the same pre-6.6.0 situation; the
tie-break is not extended to `can_reason` or to the provider-payload rungs 1-2,
where a provider's own `/models` is a statement about this deployment rather
than about the model.
